result.topic_en: Formula-only calculations on transforming the equation $\Delta\varphi=\lambda\varphi$ into new variables $\alpha,\beta$ that each satisfy a similar equation ($\Delta\alpha=\mu\alpha$, $\Delta\beta=\nu\beta$), with integrability conditions for the second derivatives of $\varphi$ and relations between gradient-squared functions of $\gamma,\gamma'$.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial z^2}=\mu\alpha$
$\frac{\partial^2\beta}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2\beta}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2\beta}{\partial z^2}=\nu\beta$
$\frac{\partial^2\varsigma}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2\varsigma}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2\varsigma}{\partial z^2}=\lambda\varsigma$

$\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\beta}\frac{\partial\beta}{\partial x}$
$\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha^2}\left(\left(\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial y}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial z}\right)^2\right)+2\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}\left([?]+[?]+[?]\right)+\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\beta^2}(\quad)+\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\alpha}\mu\alpha+\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\beta}\nu\beta=\lambda\varphi$

$\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial x}\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial y}\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial z}\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial z}=\psi(\gamma,\gamma')$

$\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial\gamma^2}\left(\frac{\partial\gamma^2}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial\gamma^2}{\partial y}\quad\right)+\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial\gamma'^2}(\quad)+\left(\frac{\partial^2\gamma'}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2\gamma'}{\partial y^2}+\cdot\right)$

$\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial\alpha}$ $\quad\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial\beta}\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial\alpha}$ $\quad\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial\beta}\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial\beta}$
$\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha^2}$ $\quad\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$ $\quad\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\beta^2}$

$\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha^2}=p\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$
$\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\beta^2}=q\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$
$\frac{\partial^3\varphi}{\partial\alpha^2\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+p\frac{\partial^3\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta^2}$
$\frac{\partial^3\varphi}{\partial\beta^2\partial\alpha}=\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}+q\frac{\partial^3\varphi}{\partial\alpha^2\partial\beta}$

$\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\beta^2}=q\,e^{\int}$
$\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}=e^{\int\frac{\left(p\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}+\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}\right)\partial\alpha+\left(q\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}\right)\partial\beta}{1-pq}}$
$\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha^2}=p\,e^{\int\frac{\left(p\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}+\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}\right)\partial\alpha+\cdots}{1-pq}}$

$[-pq\,1-]\ \frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}}{\partial\alpha}=\frac{p\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}+\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}}{1-pq}$
$\frac{\partial\log\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}}{\partial\beta}=\frac{q\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}}{1-pq}$

$p=\frac{a}{b}\quad q=\frac{c}{b}$

$[-\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}=\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}+\frac{q\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}+\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}}{1-pq}\,p\,e-]$
$[-=\frac{p\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}+\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}}{1-pq}-]$

$[-b-]\ \frac{a\frac{\partial q}{\partial\alpha}+b\frac{\partial p}{\partial\beta}}{}$
$[-a\,b\,\frac{\partial c}{\partial\alpha}-]\ \frac{a\left([-\cdot-]\frac{\partial\log q}{\partial\alpha}+b\frac{\partial\log p}{\partial\beta}\right)}{b\left(\frac{b^2}{[?]}-\frac{ac}{[?]}\right)}$

$\frac{ac\frac{\partial\log q}{\partial\alpha}+ab\frac{\partial\log p}{\partial\beta}}{b^2-ac}$

$\left(\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial x}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial y}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial z}\right)^2=\psi(\gamma,\gamma')$
$\left(\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial x}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial y}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial\gamma'}{\partial z}\right)^2=\chi(\gamma,\gamma')$

$\gamma=\varphi(\gamma')$

$\gamma-\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial x}x-\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial y}y-\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial z}z=\varsigma$
$\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial x}=p$
$\frac{\partial\gamma}{\partial y}=q$

$\sum_\iota 2\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota'}}$
$\sum 2\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial^3\alpha}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota'}^2}+2\sum_{\iota\iota'}\left(\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x_\iota\partial x_{\iota'}}\right)^2$
